name: White Reality Check benchmark gate
note: Five candidate rules are scored bar by bar against a benchmark (buy-and-hold or flat); every recheck bars a stationary-bootstrap Reality Check -- Politis-Romano blocks, ONE common index path across all rules, statistics recentred by the original sample mean -- tests the MAXIMUM of the five against the null that the best of them has no edge over the benchmark. The argmax rule is traded only while P_RC < alpha. Deviations, both for wall clock: the sample is capped at rc_n bars instead of expanding without limit, and B defaults to 200 rather than 1000. The seed is a recorded parameter.
source: White, H. (2000), 'A Reality Check for Data Snooping', Econometrica 68(5), 1097-1126 - Corollary 2.4 and Section 3 'Implementing the Bootstrap Reality Check' (P_RC = 1 - M/N, the recursive V_k updates, q=0.1, N=500-1000). PDF: https://users.ssc.wisc.edu/~bhansen/718/White2000.pdf . Applied to technical trading rules in Sullivan, R., Timmermann, A. & White, H. (1999), 'Data-Snooping, Technical Trading Rule Performance, and the Bootstrap', Journal of Finance 54(5), 1647-1691. Bootstrap: Politis, D. & Romano, J. (1994), 'The Stationary Bootstrap', JASA 89(428), 1303-1313.
code:
def _rc(P, a, m, q, B, rng):
    """One bootstrap Reality Check on the sample [a, a+m). Returns (p, kstar)."""
    import math
    L = len(P)
    sq = math.sqrt(m)
    fbar = [(P[k][a + m] - P[k][a]) / m for k in range(L)]
    kstar = 0
    for k in range(1, L):
        if fbar[k] > fbar[kstar]:
            kstar = k
    V = sq * fbar[kstar]
    if V <= 0.0:
        return 1.0, kstar          # nothing beat the benchmark, nothing to test
    lg = math.log(1.0 - q)
    ri = rng.random
    cnt = 0
    idx = range(L)
    for _ in range(B):
        tot = [0.0] * L
        filled = 0
        while filled < m:
            st = int(ri() * m)
            if st >= m:
                st = m - 1
            u = ri()
            ln = int(math.log(1.0 - u) / lg) + 1
            if ln > m - filled:
                ln = m - filled
            e = st + ln
            if e <= m:
                for k in idx:
                    Pk = P[k]
                    tot[k] += Pk[a + e] - Pk[a + st]
            else:
                wrap = e - m
                for k in idx:
                    Pk = P[k]
                    tot[k] += (Pk[a + m] - Pk[a + st]) + (Pk[a + wrap] - Pk[a])
            filled += ln
        best = None
        for k in idx:
            x = sq * (tot[k] / m - fbar[k])
            if best is None or x > best:
                best = x
        if best <= V:
            cnt += 1
    return 1.0 - cnt / float(B), kstar


def family_init(ctx):
    import random
    import indicators as I
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]

    ef = I.compute("ema", bars, period=9)["ema"]
    es = I.compute("ema", bars, period=30)["ema"]
    rs = I.compute("rsi", bars, period=14)["rsi"]
    dc = I.compute("donchian", bars, period=20)
    du, dl = dc["upper"], dc["lower"]
    sm = I.compute("sma", bars, period=20)["sma"]
    sd = I.compute("stddev", bars, period=20)["stddev"]

    # ---- the l candidate rules. Each is a POSITION decided on the close of
    # bar t and held over bar t+1. Several are near-duplicates by design --
    # that cross-rule dependence is exactly what one common bootstrap index
    # path across all rules exists to preserve.
    L = 5
    pos = [[0] * n for _ in range(L)]
    mom = 20
    for t in range(n):
        if ef[t] is not None and es[t] is not None:
            pos[0][t] = 1 if ef[t] > es[t] else -1
        if t >= mom:
            pos[1][t] = 1 if c[t] > c[t - mom] else -1
        prev = pos[2][t - 1] if t else 0
        if t and du[t - 1] is not None and dl[t - 1] is not None:
            if c[t] > du[t - 1]:
                prev = 1
            elif c[t] < dl[t - 1]:
                prev = -1
        pos[2][t] = prev
        if rs[t] is not None:
            pos[3][t] = 1 if rs[t] < 35 else (-1 if rs[t] > 65 else 0)
        if sm[t] is not None and sd[t] is not None and sd[t] > 0:
            z = (c[t] - sm[t]) / sd[t]
            pos[4][t] = -1 if z > 2.0 else (1 if z < -2.0 else 0)

    ret = [0.0] * n
    for t in range(1, n):
        ret[t] = (c[t] / c[t - 1] - 1.0) if c[t - 1] else 0.0
    use_bh = int(ctx.p.bench) == 1

    # prefix sums of the per-bar performance differential f_{k,t}
    P = []
    for k in range(L):
        pk = pos[k]
        acc = [0.0] * (n + 1)
        s = 0.0
        for t in range(n):
            f = 0.0
            if t:
                f = pk[t - 1] * ret[t] - (ret[t] if use_bh else 0.0)
            s += f
            acc[t + 1] = s
        P.append(acc)

    q = float(ctx.p.q)
    if q <= 0.0 or q >= 1.0:
        q = 0.1
    B = int(ctx.p.B)
    rc_n = int(ctx.p.rc_n)
    step = max(20, int(ctx.p.recheck))
    warm = 60
    rng = random.Random(int(ctx.p.seed))

    pv = [1.0] * n
    ks = [0] * n
    cur_p, cur_k = 1.0, 0
    nxt = warm + 200
    for t in range(n):
        if t >= nxt:
            a = t - rc_n
            if a < warm:
                a = warm
            m = t - a
            if m >= 100:
                cur_p, cur_k = _rc(P, a, m, q, B, rng)
            nxt = t + step
        pv[t] = cur_p
        ks[t] = cur_k
    ctx.pv = ctx.series(pv, "rc_p")
    ctx.kk = ctx.series(ks, "rc_kstar")
    ctx.rulepos = [ctx.series(p, "rulepos%d" % j) for j, p in enumerate(pos)]


def signal(ctx, i):
    p = ctx.pv[i]
    if p is None:
        return 0
    if p >= ctx.p.alpha:
        # the family is rejected: hold the benchmark, or stand aside
        return 1 if int(ctx.p.hold_bench) else 0
    k = ctx.kk[i]
    if k is None:
        return 0
    v = ctx.rulepos[int(k)][i]
    if not v:
        return 0
    return 1 if v > 0 else -1
